s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent episodes of loss of consciousness, visual disturbances, and headaches with associated vertigo, dizziness, and postural weakness, suggesting a complex vascular and neurological presentation
salient_findings: Recurrent blackouts
Blurring of vision and moderate frontal headaches
Vertigo, dizziness, palpitations, and postural weakness
Deficient pulses in both upper limbs
Bruit audible over the left subclavian fossa
Optic-disk cupping with irregular margins in the right eye
key_facts: Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate at 35 mm/hr
Microcytosis and hypochromasia on red-cell indices
Normal serum iron, total iron-binding capacity, transferrin, antinuclear antibodies, electrocardiogram, echocardiogram, and electroencephalogram
Computed tomography angiogram showing diffuse intimal thickening and narrowing at the origins of major arteries

shortlist.label: Takayasu arteritis
shortlist.why_kept: Diffuse intimal thickening and narrowing at the origins of major arteries, anemia, elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and age of patient

shortlist.label: Giant cell arteritis
shortlist.why_kept: Temporal headaches, visual disturbances, and elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate

shortlist.label: Polyarteritis nodosa
shortlist.why_kept: Multi-system involvement, anemia, and elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate

shortlist.label: Moyamoya disease
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent episodes of loss of consciousness, visual disturbances, and evidence of extensive collateral circulation

shortlist.label: Subclavian steal syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Bruit audible over the left subclavian fossa, deficient pulses in upper limbs, and postural weakness

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including recurrent blackouts, vertigo, and postural weakness, along with the presence of deficient pulses in both upper limbs, anemia, and a bruit over the left subclavian fossa, are consistent with large vessel vasculitis. The computed tomography angiogram showing diffuse intimal thickening and narrowing at the origins of major arteries, such as the brachiocephalic, right common carotid, and left subclavian arteries, further supports this diagnosis. Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein also indicate active inflammation, which is typical of Takayasu arteritis.

rejected.label: Giant cell arteritis
rejected.why: Typically affects older adults and is associated with jaw claudication and temporal artery tenderness, which are not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Polyarteritis nodosa
rejected.why: Usually involves smaller arteries and is associated with kidney involvement, which is not present in this case

rejected.label: Moyamoya disease
rejected.why: Characterized by stenosis or occlusion of the internal carotid artery or its branches, which is not the primary finding in this patient

rejected.label: Subclavian steal syndrome
rejected.why: Refers to a specific condition where there is reversal of blood flow in the vertebral artery due to subclavian artery stenosis, which is not the primary diagnosis given the involvement of multiple arteries
